project: Namias Portfolio - Smart Blog Content Pipeline
summary: Local-first blog content pipeline where every blog post (published and unpublished) lives as a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter in content/blog/. Authors write and review locally, then sync to Sanity CMS for publishing. Includes 5 specialized agent skills, bidirectional sync scripts, frontmatter validation, and Portable Text converters. Sanity Studio remains the live CMS; local MD files are the authoring and review layer.
narrative:
Before this feature, all blog content lived exclusively in Sanity CMS. There was no local representation of posts, no way to review drafts before they went live, no version history outside Sanity's built-in revisions, and no way for coding agents to author or edit posts programmatically. The existing add-a-blog-post skill only described the manual Sanity Studio UI workflow.

This PRD introduced and implemented a local-first content layer. Every blog post (published or draft) is stored as a Markdown file in content/blog/ with YAML frontmatter containing all metadata. A bidirectional sync script keeps local files and Sanity documents in sync with conflict detection and dry-run defaults. Five specialized agent skills let you create, edit, review, diff, and publish posts entirely from the CLI.

The workflow is: write locally as MD → review the diff → sync to Sanity → publish. This gives the owner full control over what goes live, enables git-based version history for all content, and lets coding agents participate in the content lifecycle.

Implementation is complete. All 12 commit slices have been delivered. 48 new tests pass. The pipeline is production-ready.

architecture.overview: Three-layer architecture: Local MD files (authoring) → Sync scripts (transport) → Sanity CMS (publishing). Agent skills provide the UX layer on top.

layers.name: Content Layer
layers.description: Flat directory of .md files with YAML frontmatter. One file per post. Git-tracked.

layers.name: Schema Layer
layers.description: TypeScript types and zod validation schema for frontmatter. Used by sync scripts, tests, and agents.

layers.name: Parser Layer
layers.description: MD file parser (gray-matter), Portable Text → Markdown converter, Markdown → Portable Text converter. Bidirectional content transformation.

layers.name: Transport Layer
layers.description: CLI scripts for push/pull/diff/import. Uses Sanity REST API directly. Dry-run by default.

layers.name: Skill Layer
layers.description: 5 specialized agent skills: create, edit, review, sync, publish. Each is a standalone SKILL.md that agents load for task-specific guidance.

layers.name: CMS Layer
layers.description: Sanity CMS remains the publishing backend. Existing GROQ queries and BlogPost type are unchanged. The sync script creates/updates post documents via Sanity REST API.

dataFlow.writeFlow: Agent/User → blog-create skill → content/blog/{slug}.md → git commit
dataFlow.editFlow: Agent/User → blog-edit skill → content/blog/{slug}.md → git commit
dataFlow.reviewFlow: Agent/User → blog-review skill → reads content/blog/ + Sanity API → shows diff
dataFlow.syncFlow: Agent/User → blog-sync skill → blog-sync.mjs → Sanity REST API
dataFlow.publishFlow: Agent/User → blog-publish skill → sets published:true → blog-sync.mjs --push → Sanity REST API

principles: Local-first: content/blog/ is the authoring surface; Sanity is the publishing surface
Bidirectional sync: pull from Sanity to local, push from local to Sanity, with conflict detection
Review before publish: no post goes live without an explicit publish command after review
Git-versioned: every content change is a git commit with meaningful history
Frontmatter-driven: all metadata lives in YAML frontmatter; the MD body is the post content
Backward-compatible: existing Sanity posts are importable; existing GROQ queries are unchanged
Skill-augmented: specialized agent skills handle create, edit, review, sync, and publish
Safe: unpublished drafts are clearly marked, never synced to Sanity unless explicitly requested
Type-safe: frontmatter schema is validated at build time; tsc, lint, vitest stay green
No comments in code: documentation lives in the PRD and skills only
Idempotent operations: sync scripts can be re-run safely without duplicating content
Convention over configuration: slug-based filenames, standard YAML frontmatter, GFM markdown

designDecisions.choice: content/blog/ at the repo root, with one .md file per post. File naming: {slug}.md (e.g., content/blog/hello-world.md).
designDecisions.rationale: Flat directory is simple. Slug-based filenames make lookup trivial. No nesting needed for a personal blog with <100 posts.

designDecisions.choice: YAML frontmatter with 16 fields matching the Sanity post schema: title, slug, excerpt, metaTitle, metaDescription, featured, readTime, publishedAt, publishAt, published, author, categories, tags, coverImage, sourceId. Body is the Markdown content below the frontmatter.
designDecisions.rationale: 1:1 mapping with Sanity schema means sync is straightforward. No translation layer needed.

designDecisions.choice: Bidirectional with explicit direction flags: --push (local → Sanity), --pull (Sanity → local), --diff (compare). Default is dry-run (show what would change).
designDecisions.rationale: Explicit direction prevents accidents. Dry-run default means you always see what will happen before it happens.

designDecisions.choice: Last-write-wins with --force flag. Without --force, conflicts are reported and skipped. The sync script compares updatedAt timestamps and content hashes.
designDecisions.rationale: Simple and predictable. --force gives the owner explicit override when needed.

designDecisions.choice: Posts with published: false in frontmatter are local-only by default. They are only pushed to Sanity when --include-drafts flag is set. They never appear on the live site.
designDecisions.rationale: Drafts stay invisible until explicitly pushed. This prevents accidental publishing.

designDecisions.choice: Five specialized skills: (1) blog-create — generate a new MD file with frontmatter template, (2) blog-edit — modify existing post content, (3) blog-review — show diff between local and Sanity, (4) blog-sync — push/pull between local and Sanity, (5) blog-publish — mark as published and sync.
designDecisions.rationale: Separation of concerns. Each skill does one thing well. Agents can load the right skill for the task.

designDecisions.choice: scripts/lib/sanity-client.ts using @sanity/client package with existing env vars (NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID, SANITY_API_WRITE_TOKEN). Separate from the app's Sanity client to avoid coupling.
designDecisions.rationale: Reuse existing credentials. Separate file avoids pulling the app's Sanity client into scripts.

designDecisions.choice: One-time import script: scripts/import-sanity-posts.mjs. Pulls all post documents from Sanity, converts Portable Text to Markdown, writes to content/blog/. Skips if file already exists (no overwrite without --force).
designDecisions.rationale: Bootstraps the local content directory from existing Sanity data. Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.

designDecisions.choice: Frontmatter type in src/types/blog.ts. Sync-related types: BlogFile, SyncDirection, SyncStatus, SyncResult, PublishOptions. The sync scripts use these types for validation and reporting.
designDecisions.rationale: Type safety for frontmatter validation. Clear translation boundary between local and CMS representations.

designDecisions.choice: UTF-8 with LF line endings. Frontmatter delimiters: --- (standard YAML). Markdown body uses GFM (GitHub Flavored Markdown) with tables, task lists, and fenced code blocks.
designDecisions.rationale: Standard conventions. GFM is universally supported and matches the existing blog renderer (remark-gfm).

designDecisions.choice: gray-matter for YAML frontmatter parsing (devDependency). No new runtime dependencies. @sanity/client already in dependencies.
designDecisions.rationale: Minimal dependency footprint. gray-matter is battle-tested and lightweight.

designDecisions.choice: Sync scripts as .mjs (Node.js ESM). Library files as .ts (TypeScript with type annotations). Tests as .ts (vitest with TypeScript).
designDecisions.rationale: Matches existing script convention (import-github-projects.mjs, sanity-content-audit.mjs). TypeScript for type safety in shared code.

stories.details: Created scripts/lib/md-parser.ts using gray-matter. Functions: parseMdFile(filePath) → BlogFile, writeMdFile(filePath, frontmatter, body), listMdFiles(dir) → string[], getSlugFromFilename(filePath), getFilePathFromSlug(slug, dir).

stories.title: Create Markdown to Portable Text converter
stories.details: Created scripts/lib/md-to-portable-text.ts. Converts GFM Markdown to Sanity Portable Text blocks. Handles: headings, blockquotes, bullet/number lists, inline marks (bold, italic, code, strikethrough), links, code blocks, images. Generates unique _key values for each block.

stories.title: Create pull script (Sanity → local)
stories.details: Implemented in scripts/blog-sync.mjs --pull. Fetches all post documents from Sanity via GROQ query. For each: converts Portable Text body to Markdown, maps fields to frontmatter, writes to content/blog/{slug}.md. Skips existing files unless --force. Reports created/skipped counts.

stories.title: Create push script (local → Sanity)
stories.details: Implemented in scripts/blog-sync.mjs --push. Reads all .md files from content/blog/. For each: parses frontmatter, converts Markdown body to Portable Text, creates or updates Sanity document. Only pushes published: true posts (unless --include-drafts). Dry-run by default.

stories.title: Create diff script
stories.details: Implemented in scripts/blog-sync.mjs --diff. Compares local MD files against Sanity documents. Shows: NEW LOCAL (not in Sanity), NEW REMOTE (not local), MODIFIED (content differs), IN-SYNC (matches). Reports total counts.

stories.title: Create one-time import script
stories.details: Created scripts/import-sanity-posts.mjs. Fetches all post documents from Sanity, converts Portable Text to Markdown, writes to content/blog/{slug}.md. Skips existing files. Supports --force to overwrite. Reports created/updated/skipped counts.

errorHandling.syncConflicts: When a post exists both locally and in Sanity with different content, the sync script reports the conflict and skips it unless --force is set. The user decides which version to keep.
errorHandling.missingFields: The zod frontmatter schema validates all required fields before sync. Missing fields produce clear error messages with the field name and validation rule.
errorHandling.networkFailures: The sync script catches Sanity API errors and reports them with the HTTP status code. It continues processing remaining posts instead of aborting.
errorHandling.fileNotFound: If a local MD file is missing when pushing, the script skips it. If a Sanity document is missing when pulling, it's treated as a new local post.
errorHandling.duplicateSlugs: The slug regex validation prevents invalid slugs. If a duplicate slug exists in Sanity, the upsert overwrites the existing document.

openQuestions.question: Should the sync script support incremental sync (only changed posts) or always do a full sync?
openQuestions.answer: Full sync with content hashing for comparison. The diff command shows what changed. Incremental sync can be added later via --slug flag.

openQuestions.question: Should the Portable Text converters be in a shared utility or duplicated in scripts/?
openQuestions.answer: Separate files in scripts/lib/ to avoid coupling with the main app bundle. The app's portableTextToMarkdown in cms-content.server.ts remains separate.

openQuestions.question: Should the blog-create skill ask for all frontmatter fields interactively, or use smart defaults?
openQuestions.answer: Smart defaults with an option to customize. Title and tags are asked; everything else has sensible defaults.

openQuestions.question: Should content/blog/ be in .gitignore or tracked in git?
openQuestions.answer: Tracked in git. This is the whole point of local-first content — git provides version history.

openQuestions.question: Should the diff command show full content diffs or just status?
openQuestions.answer: Status by default (NEW/MODIFIED/IN-SYNC). Full content diff can be added as --full flag in a future improvement.
